intro.lead: How a new merchant signs up on Wire, completes verification, creates a project and activates an operator connection — the full sequence, with real screens.

signup.title: Sign-up and verification
signup.intro: Wire has no separate password — you sign in with an email code, your phone, Google or DAN (state e-ID). Because this is a financial service for taking payments, every owner completes three verifications in this order: email, phone, DAN; the one you signed in with already counts. Each is done once — however many businesses or projects you open, they are not asked again.

project.title: Create a project
project.intro: Business = the identity with KYC, bank accounts and operator registrations. Project = the integration environment under it: its own API key, one webhook and a checkout template. One business can have many projects, and one user can open several businesses.

connector.title: Connect an operator
connector.intro: To take payments, connect at least one payment operator to your business. The flow: fill in and submit the form → review and approval → sign the agreement electronically → payments go live. The agreement is signed after approval — submitting the application needs no agreement. Operator names and numbers are generalised in the screenshots below — your account shows the real names of the operators active for it.

integration.title: Integration settings
integration.intro: Once an operator is active, these two things are needed for a technical integration. You can start using payment links and checkout right away, without writing code.

s1.title: Choose how to sign in
s1.desc: Go to app.wire.mn and choose how to sign in: a one-time code by email, your phone, Google or DAN. If this is your first sign-in, a new account is created automatically.
s1.caption: app.wire.mn/signin — the sign-in page

s2.title: Enter your phone number
s2.desc: A new user goes straight to the verification page. The first step, email, is confirmed with a 6-digit code — if you signed in by email or Google, it is already done. Then enter your phone number and click <ui>Verify</ui>.
s2.caption: Verification 2/3 — phone number

s3.title: Verify by sending an SMS
s3.desc: Send the code shown on screen by SMS from your own phone to the short number given — you send it yourself instead of waiting for a message. Once it is sent, the page continues automatically.
s3.caption: Code + short number, waiting for the SMS

s4.title: Start DAN verification
s4.desc: The third step — verify your personal details through the state DAN system. Click <ui>Verify with DAN</ui>.
s4.caption: Verification 3/3 — DAN

s5.title: Give consent on sso.gov.mn
s5.desc: You move to the state single sign-on, sign in with your own DAN account and consent to sharing your details. When it succeeds, you return automatically.
s5.caption: DAN — the state identity and sign-in system

s6.title: Check that you are verified
s6.desc: On the profile page, check that email, phone and DAN all show <ui>Verified</ui>. From here on, every feature is open.
s6.caption: Profile — fully verified

s7.title: Create a new project — give it a name
s7.desc: In the project switcher at the top left, click <ui>Create new project</ui>. Give it a name and choose the business option. Your first project does not show this choice — its business is created along with it.
s7.caption: Use the current business (default) — registration, accounts and connections carry over

s8.title: Or: register a new business
s8.desc: To open a brand-new business for a separate legal entity or another line of activity, take the second option. Email, phone and DAN are not asked again; KYC, bank accounts and operator applications run separately on the new business.
s8.caption: Register a new business — its own KYC, accounts and applications

s9.title: Store your secret key
s9.desc: As soon as the project is created, the sk_live_… secret key is shown only once. Save it in a password manager with the Copy or Download .txt button — it is never shown again; if you lose it, create a new key.
s9.caption: One-time key reveal (the key in the image is invalid)

s10.title: Project overview
s10.desc: The new project's home. The left menu leads to transactions, payment links, checkout, accounts, reports and settings.
s10.caption: Overview — a new project's start

s11.title: Choose from the Connections page
s11.desc: Settings → Channels. Choose which of the operators active for your account to connect. One project can connect several operators, each operator once.
s11.caption: Connections — the list of available operators (names generalised)

s12.title: Start and the fast track
s12.desc: The operator page shows progress in 3 stages. If you were approved before on another business, a <ui>Use your existing merchant registration</ui> card appears — choose it and the connection works right away, with no new application and no wait. For a new business, fill in the 5-step form (Individual / Organisation).
s12.caption: The 3 progress stages, the existing-registration card, step 1 of the form (operator No. hidden)

s13.title: Form 2/5 — Basic details
s13.desc: Register number, surname and name, business name, type of activity. The <ui>Use</ui> button on the <ui>Fill with DAN-verified details</ui> card fills them in one click.
s13.caption: 2/5 Details — DAN prefill (register number hidden)

s14.title: Form 3/5 — Address and contact
s14.desc: City, district, full address, phone, email. You can also fill these in one click from your DAN address and your profile details.
s14.caption: 3/5 Address — two prefill cards (address hidden)

s15.title: Form 4/5 — Settlement account
s15.desc: Choose the bank account where your revenue lands, or add a new one with <ui>Connect another account</ui>. Accounts you connected before are already listed.
s15.caption: 4/5 Account (number hidden)

s16.title: Form 5/5 — Review and submit
s16.desc: Check all your details on one screen and click <ui>Submit request</ui>. The form saves itself at every step, so you can leave it half done and continue later.
s16.caption: 5/5 Review — summary (personal details hidden)

s17.title: Confirm the submission
s17.desc: Click <ui>Submit</ui> in the last window and the request goes to review.
s17.caption: The Submit request? window — final confirmation

s18.title: Review → agreement → activation
s18.desc: The request moves to Under review. Once it is approved, you get an email and a section to sign the agreement electronically appears on the operator page — as soon as you sign it, the connection goes live and you start taking payments.
s18.caption: A request under review — you can cancel it and submit again

s19.title: Manage API keys
s19.desc: Settings → API key. Rotate a key and revoke the old one. Each key reaches only its own project's data.
s19.caption: API key — each project has its own sk_live key

s20.title: Connect a webhook
s20.desc: Settings → Webhook. Register the URL of the server that receives payment events and verify it. Each project has exactly one webhook endpoint; when you change the URL, events keep going to the old address until the new one is verified. Full API reference — docs.wire.mn.
s20.caption: Webhook — register and verify an endpoint

notes.s8: If you chose the wrong option: a project with no data can move to another business through the <ui>Use your existing merchant registration</ui> card on the operator page (step 12).
notes.s18: Note: even after approval, the connection stays inactive until you sign the agreement. The most common reason an approved connection does not work is that the agreement step was not done.

terms.heading: Terms of service.
terms.lead: By signing up and signing in to Wire, you accept the terms below.

service.title: 1. Service
service.body: Wire (wire.mn) is a payment gateway that connects Mongolia's payment operators through one integration. Through the dashboard you take payments, track your transactions and manage your settings.

account.title: 2. Account and sign-in
account.body: Sign-in is passwordless — you sign in with a one-time code sent to your email, an SMS code from your phone, a Google account or DAN (state e-ID). We do not store passwords. Each email address, phone number and DAN belongs to only one person, and whichever method you use, you sign in to the same account.

kyc.title: 3. Verification (KYC)
kyc.body: Because this is a financial service, every owner verifies (a) their email address with a one-time code or a Google account, (b) their phone number by SMS and (c) their personal details through the state DAN e-ID system (sso.gov.mn). The details received from DAN (name, register number, address) are stored encrypted. One citizen can verify only one account.

privacy.title: 4. Data protection
privacy.body: Personal and bank account details are stored with AES-256 encryption. We do not use your data for advertising and do not sell it to third parties. We share it with payment operators only as far as the merchant registration requires.

payments.title: 5. Payment data
payments.body: Transaction amounts, statuses and related metadata are kept for reconciliation and dispute resolution. All amounts are recorded in tögrög (MNT).

duties.title: 6. User obligations
duties.body: Keep your API keys secret. Using Wire to take payments for illegal goods or services is prohibited. If a violation is found, the account may be suspended or closed permanently.

termination.title: 7. Termination
termination.body: You can delete your projects and leave the service at any time. Under financial record-keeping laws and regulations, some transaction history is kept for the required period.

intro.lead: Wire is a financial service for taking payments. That is why every account opening includes email, phone and personal identity verification — <hl>it protects you and your customers</hl>.

email.copy: Enter your address and a 6-digit code arrives — <hl>type it in and you are verified</hl>. If you signed in by email or Google, this step is already done.

bullets.valid: The code is valid for 10 minutes
bullets.notices: Application answers and payment notifications go to this address

phone.copy: Enter your number and <hl>send one SMS to the given short number — that verifies it</hl>. No code to remember and no app to install — the message sent from your own phone is the proof.

bullets.alerts: Notifications and important alerts go to this number

dan.copy: You move to DAN (sso.gov.mn), the state single sign-on, and sign in with your own consent. <hl>Wire never sees your password</hl> — only the verified result (name, register number) reaches us.

bullets.official: An official state system — no extra documents to send
bullets.signed: A signed channel — data cannot be altered in transit

encrypted.title: Encrypted storage
encrypted.desc: Personal data is encrypted with AES-256. The screen shows only your name and the first and last parts of your register number (masked).

oneCitizen.title: One citizen = one account
oneCitizen.desc: One citizen's details can verify only one account — this prevents duplicate sign-ups and fraud.

noThirdParty.title: Not shared with third parties
noThirdParty.desc: We do not use your data for advertising and do not sell it. It is used only as far as KYC requires.

status.heading: System status.
status.footer: Systems are checked live every time you reload this page. If an outage continues, write to <link>{email}</link>.
